limitations: Registry attributes are current-vintage weekly-snapshot values applied retrospectively to inspections as far back as 2010; this is retrospective research and does not establish the operational record on the inspection date.
RCRA_FACILITIES.csv covers handlers in the current reporting universe, so the panel is subject to registry survivorship rather than inspection survivorship.

FOUND_VIOLATION reflects state coding and inspection intensity as well as facility conduct; state and inspecting agency are available but residual confounding remains and the label is not a uniform national standard.

The current extract contains a found-violation code outside the publisher-documented Yes, Undetermined and No set. Its meaning is not established; it is excluded as unclassified and never treated as a negative.
Violation determinations may post-date the inspection by weeks because they can follow sampling results or legal review, so the outcome is short-horizon rather than instantaneous.

Dropping Undetermined, blank and unclassified found-violation rows is selection on label availability; the build reports those shares because states that code many evaluations that way will be under-represented.
One earliest CEI per handler approximates independence; handlers whose only in-window CEI falls in an embargo gap are removed from all splits.

Prior violations, prior evaluations, SNC status and VIOSNC monthly flags are excluded because they are rolling histories of the same target and would create cross-row leakage; their absence caps achievable signal.
Facility names and street addresses are excluded from features; the released table carries handler identifiers but no names.
No historical registry vintage ledger or exact publication schedule was available, so feature availability and training label timing remain unverified rather than documented.

task.decision_user: State or EPA RCRA enforcement program manager allocating scarce inspection capacity, and an inspector preparing the scheduled inspection.
task.outcome_horizon: The finding attached to that single evaluation; the violation determination date is not necessarily the inspection date and may follow sampling or legal review by roughly weeks.
task.population: RCRA_EVALUATIONS.csv rows with EVALUATION_TYPE equal to CEI, a parseable EVALUATION_START_DATE inside one of the three frozen windows, FOUND_VIOLATION in the Yes or No code, and a matching ID_NUMBER plus ACTIVITY_LOCATION in RCRA_FACILITIES.csv; only the earliest qualifying CEI per ID_NUMBER is retained. The current extract also carries an undocumented found-violation code, which is excluded as unclassified rather than mapped to either label.
task.prediction_time: 00:00 local time on EVALUATION_START_DATE, the first day of the inspection or record review, before any site visit, record request or observation.
task.question: A hazardous-waste handler is scheduled for a routine RCRA compliance evaluation inspection. Before the inspector arrives, will that inspection record at least one violation?
task.simple_references: Majority class, state base-rate lookup, HREPORT-universe lookup, inspection-month calendar control, and an Operating-TSDF identity control.
task.split_policy: Frozen on EVALUATION_START_DATE: training window starts 2010-01-01 inclusive and ends 2023-07-01 exclusive; evaluation window 2023-07-31 to 2024-07-01; holdout window 2024-07-31 to 2025-07-31; the 30-day gaps after each boundary are excluded; one handler contributes at most one row.
task.title: Will a routine hazardous-waste compliance evaluation inspection find a violation at a U.S. handler?
task.usefulness: The label is not recoverable from registry attributes: the task measures how much violation risk is predictable from facility universe, generator size, industry, state and inspecting agency before a visit.

prediction_instant.citation: EPA RCRAInfo data element dictionary: the evaluation date is the first day of the inspection or record review

row_selection.rule: earliest CEI per ID_NUMBER within the three frozen half-open windows
